summary: This bill amends federal law to require states to hold special elections filling any House vacancy within 180 days after it occurs (unless a general election falls in that window) and authorizes the Attorney General plus aggrieved parties to sue state officials for enforcement.

scores.thoughts: The bill addresses only the timing of special elections for House vacancies and contains no provisions related to federal or state budgets, appropriations, or expenditures.
The bill contains no tax-related provisions of any kind.

The bill directly amends federal law to require states to hold special elections for House vacancies within 180 days (unless a general election falls inside that window) and authorizes civil enforcement actions by the Attorney General and private parties. This constitutes election-procedure reform aimed at ensuring timely representation and preventing extended vacancies, which aligns with the 'expand voting access and election reform' direction of the scale.
No technology, data-privacy, or regulatory provisions are included.
The bill does not address labor, employment, or union issues.
No religious-liberty or anti-discrimination provisions appear.
